chunks: And from him, from Yahya ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Zakat is permissible for the owner of the house and the servant,' because Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) did not consider the house and the servant to be anything (i.e., not separate entities distinct from the owner).
ai.seo_question: Who is eligible to receive zakat according to the reasoning of Imam al-Sadiq regarding householders and servants?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a recipient of zakat is not disqualified by owning a residence or a servant, as these are considered functional necessities rather than surplus wealth. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that 'wealth' (mal) for zakat eligibility refers to disposable assets, distinguishing between essential living quarters and investable capital. It underscores the practical flexibility in zakat distribution to ensure support reaches those with basic needs despite modest household holdings.
